mmff94_term_audit_summary.generated_from: crates/chematic-3d/examples/mmff94_term_coverage_audit.rs (fresh re-run, Priority 2B: RDKit's Dfsb periodic-row stretch-bend fallback ported into PRODUCTION chematic_ff::mmff94_stbn)
mmff94_term_audit_summary.note: Two SEPARATE axes, deliberately not collapsed into one (review-driven fix): (1) TYPE-ONLY diagnostic ('by_term_kind' below, using mmff94_stbn_type_only, independent of Dfsb) -- 'routing_bug_candidate' = a table row exists at a *different* classification code (classification-derivation bug candidate), 'table_gap' = absent at *every* code (genuine table gap). (2) FINAL PRODUCTION RESOLUTION ('stretch_bend_dfsb_resolution' below) -- coverage parity (does *some* value get returned) is NOT the same question as parameter-selection parity (is the *correct* value being used). A StretchBend routing_bug_candidate that Dfsb also resolves is MASKED, not fixed -- its real, correctly-typed parameter is hidden behind RDKit's generic periodic-row default instead. For Bond/Angle/Torsion/Oop, table_gap is not further sub-classified (chematic-ff implements neither equivalence-class substitution nor empirical-rule estimation for those term kinds) -- deferred, not fabricated.

stretch_bend_dfsb_resolution.note: dfsb_resolved_routing_candidate = a routing-bug candidate (real parameter exists at a different classification code) that Dfsb ALSO happens to resolve -- coverage achieved, but chematic is using RDKit's generic default instead of the correctly-routed specific parameter; NOT fixed, just no longer visible as 'missing'. dfsb_resolved_true_type_table_gap = a genuine table gap (absent at every classification code) that Dfsb resolves -- this IS the case Dfsb was built to close, matching RDKit's own real behavior exactly. final_unresolved = neither chematic's type table nor the Dfsb fallback resolves this -- 0 in this corpus.
